newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: NLCF's '96 feed grain, oilseed imports up 21.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: NLCF's '96 feed grain, oilseed imports up 21.7 pct.

text.p: South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) said on Friday its feed grain and oilseed imports would total 3,768,654 tonnes in calendar 1996, up 21.7 percent from 3,096,600 tonnes in 1995.
But in value, its imports would amount to $661.5 million this year, up 57.3 percent from $420.5 million last year, an official at the federation's purchasing department said.
The figures are based on the delivery schedule.
"We were the second-largest buyer of feed grains and oilseeds in the world," the official said.
Despite the overall increase in feed grain and oilseed imports, corn imports would fall 11.6 percent to 1.93 million tonnes from 2.18 million tonnes in 1995, he said.
"Corn imports fell mainly because of high prices," he said.
The majority of its corn imports would come from the United States, with the remainder coming from Argentina, the official said.
Its feed wheat imports would total 211,000 tonnes from none last year and rye imports would surge 163 percent to 529,954 tonnes from 201,650 tonnes. All rye imports are from Europe.
India was the biggest supplier of feed wheat, making up 75.4 percent of the total imports with the United States suppling the remainder.
Soybean meal imports would reach 243,719 tonnes this year, up 50 percent from 162,996 tonnes in 1995.

Rapeseed meal imports will total 145,688 tonnes, cottonseed meal imports 100,111 tonnes, palm kernel meal 76,144 tonnes, tapioca pellets 150,175 tonnes, wheat bran pellets 207,242 tonnes, rice bran pellets 103,941 tonnes, alfalfa pellets 32,085 tonnes and imports of other items 41,743 tonnes.
